chunks.arabic_text: عَمَّارُ بْنُ مَرْوَانَ، الثَّوْبَانِيُّ، مَوْلَى بَنِي ثَوْبَانَ مَوَالِي بَنِي يَشْكُرَ، كُوفِيٌّ. يَرْوِي عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, al-Thawbānī, client of the Banū Thawbān (clients of the Banū Yashkur), Kufan. He narrates from Abū al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry identifies ʿAmmār ibn Marwān al-Thawbānī as a Kufan narrator who transmitted traditions from Imam al-Riḍā (AS) and Imam al-Jawād (AS), placing him within the crucial transitional period of the Minor Occultation. His affiliation with the Mawālī of Banī Yashkur highlights the significant role of non-Arab converts in preserving and transmitting Imami hadith during the formative centuries of Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAmmār ibn Marwān al-Thawbānī and who did he narrate from?

key_terms.الثَّوْبَانِيُّ: Al-Thawbānī: A nisba indicating affiliation with the Thawban tribe or family.
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Mawlā: Client or freedman, indicating a social or legal relationship of patronage.
key_terms.بَنِي يَشْكُرَ: Banū Yashkur: A specific tribe or clan, here mentioned as the patrons of the Banū Thawbān.
key_terms.كُوفِيٌّ: Kufāwī: Denoting origin from the city of Kufa in Iraq.
key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan: A common kunya for Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (AS) or Imam al-Riḍā (AS).
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh: A common kunya for Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (AS) or Imam al-Ḥusayn (AS).
